name: Forza Horizon 2
summary: The Xbox One edition of Forza Horizon 2 on SteamOS, through the Azimuth launcher.
description:
Azimuth is a wrapper that runs the Xbox One version of Forza Horizon 2 on Windows (and on SteamOS through Proton). It translates the Xbox WinRT calls to Win32 and Xbox DirectX 11.X to desktop DirectX 12. The supported version of the game is 1.0.0.64.

Azimuth is lightweight and reaches 720p60 or 1080p30 on a Steam Deck, so hardware on par or faster with 16 GB of RAM should be good to go.

Main features:
• Resolutions from 720p up to whatever your display uses
• 30 or 60 fps
• Three graphics modes: Low (lower than Xbox One, close to the game's split-screen profile), Default (Xbox One level) and High (shadows and reflections twice as detailed, shadows drawn three times as far, car models from photo mode, 16× anisotropic filtering)
• Anti-aliasing: off, MSAA ×2 or MSAA ×4

piShop points Azimuth at the game's files for you, so the launcher doesn't ask for the folder at the first start. Its settings live in azimuth.ini, in the game's folder.
steamos: Controller ignored at “Press A”: on Linux/Proton, Azimuth 0.9.7 only reads the first controller slot. An always-connected generic USB receiver (DragonRise) takes it and your controller is ignored. Turn on “Ignore a generic USB receiver” in Games → Patches.
Stutters or slowdowns: keep the frame rate locked at 30 fps (frame_rate=30 in azimuth.ini, Azimuth's default).

patches.title: Ignore a generic USB receiver
patches.about: Azimuth only reads the first controller slot. An always-connected generic receiver (DragonRise, USB 0079:0006) takes it, and your controller is ignored at “Press A”. Sets SDL_GAMECONTROLLER_IGNORE_DEVICES=0x0079/0x0006.
